Quick technical read:
- Latency SLA: for their described workload (short-generation, <256 tokens, high QPS) we can commit to P50 <40ms and P95 <120ms on our Dedicated offering assuming they accept the recommended batching window; for hosted it’s slightly higher but still competitive. I recommend we offer a conditional SLA: baseline SLA with an SLA uplift addendum for the first 90 days tied to their pilot acceptance criteria.
- SRE effort: With a small automation module (CI/CD runbook + one offboarding script) we can keep hands-on SRE time to ~10–12 engineer-hours for the cutover. If they want Redwood-managed infra (Dedicated), that drops to ~4–6 hours.
- Rollback checklist: we can produce a one-page rollback that maps Redwood endpoints back to VectorScale endpoints and includes KV cache flush guidance; that’s straightforward.

Risk tradeoff: we can shorten pilot credits to 6 weeks if we get a commitment to a 12-month term at a modest tiered discount (15% for months 1–3, 10% for months 4–6). That keeps our payback window tight and gives the customer clear economics.

Happy to join the customer call.

— Jonas
